caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular, walled garden divided into geometric sections with paths running vertically and horizontally, forming a grid. The garden is colored mainly in green, brown, and beige, representing plants, soil, and pathways. At the top of the garden within the walls, there are two structures: one is a white house with a red roof in the center, and the other is a small white building with a blue pointed roof on the right. The upper half of the garden contains two large, beige rectangular plots filled with evenly spaced green trees or shrubs. Below these, four rectangular plots are divided by paths, with the two on the left and right featuring symmetrical, ornate, green landscaping with decorative patterns. The lower half of the garden is split into smaller rectangular and square beds, each containing different arrangements of green and brown plantings. The central paths connect to a brown gate at the bottom middle, depicted within a fence or wall. Above the garden is a circular emblem containing a red and black shield with three white X-shaped crosses and decorative banners. At the bottom of the page is a ribbon banner with the text “DUTCH WEST INDIA COMPANY EXPERIMENTAL GARDEN.” The artist’s signature, "HELEN R. MILLER," appears in the lower right corner of the drawing.
title: Dutch West India Company
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
